title: Chef Kunal Kapur Shares Easy Vegan Mango Almond Milk Pudding Recipe
excerpt: The MasterChef India judge's no-bake, eggless dessert uses homemade almond milk and fresh mangoes — and takes just 30 minutes of active work.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Chef Kunal Kapur's pudding is a vegan, no-bake dessert using homemade almond milk and fresh mangoes.
  • The recipe serves four and requires 30 minutes of preparation plus one hour of refrigeration.
  • All ingredients are easily found in Western grocery stores, catering to the Indian diaspora.
  • The pudding is gluten-free and ideal for gatherings with diverse dietary preferences.
  • Mango season runs from May to August, making this dessert timely for summer occasions.
Quick & Easy Vegan Dessert
30 minutes
Active Preparation Time
4
Servings
1 hour
Refrigeration Time
¾ cup
Almonds Needed
2½ cups
Water for Almond Milk

Chef Kunal Kapur's no-bake mango almond milk pudding requires no oven, no eggs, and no dairy — just ripe mangoes, a handful of almonds, and 30 minutes of active work.

The MasterChef India host and judge shared the recipe on his website chefkunalkapur.com, billing it as a vegan, gluten-free dessert suited for summer entertaining. The pudding, which serves four, relies on homemade almond milk thickened with cornstarch and topped with a fresh mango sauce.

How to Make It

The recipe starts from scratch — no store-bought almond milk required. Kapur calls for soaking ¾ cup of almonds (about 110 grams), blending them with 2½ cups of water, and straining the mixture through a fine mesh bag. The result is roughly 500 ml of fresh almond milk with a richer flavor than packaged alternatives.

A portion of the almond milk is whisked with 35 grams of cornflour to create a slurry, while the rest goes into a saucepan with 100 grams of sugar and a whole cinnamon stick. Once the saucepan mixture reaches a boil, the cornstarch slurry is whisked in and cooked until the mixture reaches a thick, gooey consistency. A few drops of vanilla essence round out the base before it is poured into molds and refrigerated for at least one hour.

The mango sauce is equally straightforward: one large mango, 50 grams of sugar, 1½ cups of water, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Mint sprigs finish the plate.

A Dessert Built for the Diaspora Kitchen

For Indians abroad, the recipe addresses a common frustration: craving a familiar mango-based dessert without access to the full Indian pantry. Unlike kulfi or mango phirni — both of which require dairy and extended preparation — Kapur's pudding uses pantry staples found at any Western grocery store. Almonds, cornstarch, sugar, vanilla essence, and mangoes are available year-round in most North American and European supermarkets.

The recipe's vegan and dairy-free profile also makes it practical for potlucks and gatherings with mixed dietary preferences — a growing consideration for diaspora families navigating lactose intolerance, veganism, and varied food restrictions among friends and colleagues.

Mango season runs from roughly May through August in the diaspora's key geographies — the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and the Middle East — making this a timely addition to the summer dessert rotation.

Ingredients at Your Fingertips
›Homemade almond milk
›Fresh mangoes
›Cornstarch for thickening
›Sugar and vanilla essence

About Chef Kunal Kapur

Kapur, born in 1979 in New Delhi, is one of India's most recognized culinary figures. He hosted and judged MasterChef India across Seasons 1, 2, 3, and 5, and was invited to judge the semi-final of MasterChef America Season 2 alongside Gordon Ramsay, according to The Better India. His career began with the Taj Group of Hotels around 2000, and he later served as Executive Sous Chef at The Leela Kempinski in Gurgaon.

He has since opened restaurants including Pincode, Quarter Plate, and Patiala by Kunal Kapur in Dubai. His YouTube channel has become a major platform for recipes spanning traditional Indian curries to globally inspired dishes like this pudding.

"The best of Indian food is still trapped in the home kitchen."

— Kunal Kapur, in an interview with Slurrp

What's Next

Kapur has been posting a series of summer-appropriate recipes on his website, including Bharwa Karela with Raw Mango and Masala Shikanji four ways. A full video tutorial for the mango almond pudding is available on his YouTube channel. With mango season peaking across South Asia and diaspora markets alike, more seasonal dessert recipes from the chef are expected through August.
